sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

Convention between France and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2008, as amended)
Convention between France and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2013)
Accord entre le Gouvernement de la République française et le Gouvernement de la Région administrative spéciale de Hong Kong pour l'évitement des doubles impositions (2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II), Articles R.561-1 and R.561-16 regarding the UBO register, Decree No. 2017-1390 of 22 September 2017, Directive (EU) 2015/849 as transposed, and Arrêté of 2 September 2020 on the format of UBO declaration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate extract from the foreign registry of the ultimate shareholder (Extrait K-bis or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the French incorporation agent or counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each beneficial owner and corporate officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consular authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or financial standing certificate for the proposed SAS capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank established in the country of origin or in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the French national sanctions list (Direction Générale du Trésor), EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions, and PEP categories as defined under French law and FATF recommendations. Risk-based due diligence is conducted under Articles L.561-5 to L.561-7 of the Monetary and Financial Code, including identity verification of natural persons, UBO identification, and activity risk assessment for the low-risk POD retail segment, with enhanced monitoring if transactions involve high-risk jurisdictions or inconsistent volumes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) via infogreffe.fr and the INPI data portal for trademark pre-verification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in French or, if a foreign name is used, must be transliterated into Latin script and must be sufficiently distinctive to avoid confusion with existing registered names. The name must not be contrary to public order or morality and must respect French linguistic provisions on consumer information under Articles L.121-1 et seq. of the Consumer Code.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection notification from the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, the applicant may within 15 days submit a reasoned request for reconsideration accompanied by additional distinguishing elements, a trademark coexistence agreement, or a waiver from the relevant ministerial authority if a sensitive token is involved. If the rejection is based on trademark opposition or prior identical name, the applicant may file a substantive response with evidence of prior usage or a consent letter. Further recourse may be brought before the Directeur général de l'INPI within two months under Article L.712-2 of the Intellectual Property Code, and ultimately before the competent commercial court through a declaratory action or an application for review, with judicial filing within one month of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for an SAS engaged in POD retail only if the registered address is a physical premises in France under a written domiciliation contract with an approved commercial domiciliation provider (domiciliataire), the contract is filed with the Greffe, and the registered address is not a mere PO box. The registered office must be capable of receiving official correspondence and may be subject to verification; full virtual substance without any operational anchor in France is not permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk; approximately 5% annual likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspection for low-risk e-commerce registrations, increasing to 15-25% if the domiciliation provider is placed under administrative monitoring or if anomalies appear in tax or UBO filings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee for single corporate name search across RCS and INPI databases

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate per page and statutory certification fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company provisions), L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée regime), and R.123-103 et seq. (RCS registration); Code civil Articles 1845 et seq.; loi PACTE n° 2019-486 and its implementing regulations (Guichet Unique electronic filing); Code monétaire et financier Article L.561-2-1 (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the department of the registered office, receiving the file through the national one-stop electronic portal 'Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises' operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Single electronic registration dossier (formulaire M0) transmitted via the Guichet Unique, comprising the signed Articles of Association (Statuts), the capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds), the legal announcement certificate (attestation de parution), the beneficial-owner declaration (DBE), and all supporting corporate documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum share capital for an SAS (capital freely set in the Statuts, typically EUR 1); at least 50% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation and the full cash capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a French bank or a notary until RCS registration; in-kind contributions must be fully transferred at incorporation; the balance of cash contributions may be settled within five years.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-resident businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). Official portal: https://www.impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and statutory business-registration formalities are filed through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), which transmits registration data for allocation of the SIREN and SIRET identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS: (1) complete incorporation formalities through the INPI Guichet unique; (2) obtain the SIREN and SIRET identifiers from the national business register; (3) identify the competent SIE based on the registered office; (4) submit the tax registration information and beneficial-owner, activity, bank-account, accounting-period, and establishment details requested by the DGFiP; (5) request or confirm the French intra-Community VAT number, normally beginning with FR and containing a two-character key followed by the nine-digit SIREN; and (6) activate the professional account on impots.gouv.fr for tax filings and electronic correspondence. A foreign entity carrying on taxable transactions in France without a French establishment applies to the SIEE for a French VAT number. An entity established in another EU Member State generally does not appoint a French tax representative solely for French VAT registration. A non-EU entity generally must appoint an accredited French tax representative under Article 289 A of the French Tax Code, unless an applicable exemption applies. The application should include constitutional documents, certificate of tax residence, evidence of business activity, identification of directors and beneficial owners, power of attorney, French establishment or customer details, expected transaction flows, customs activity, and banking information. VAT identification does not replace customs EORI registration, which is required for relevant import and export operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level. There is no United States-style check-the-box election. A qualifying SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime for up to five financial years under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, subject to statutory conditions concerning size, age, ownership, management, non-listing, and business activity; the election must be filed within the applicable deadline and is generally irrevocable once exercised. A qualifying group may elect the French VAT group regime where the required financial, economic, and organizational links exist. French and EU anti-hybrid-mismatch rules apply by operation of law; there is no general elective hybrid-mismatch classification. Tax treaties and permanent-establishment rules may modify the allocation of taxing rights for non-French owners or activities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT. French VAT applies to taxable supplies made in France, intra-Community transactions under the applicable EU VAT rules, imports, and certain electronically supplied or distance-sale transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover threshold allowing a taxable established SAS to avoid VAT registration where it makes transactions giving rise to VAT obligations. The French franchise en base regime may apply below the applicable thresholds, subject to activity and transaction-type rules. The commonly applicable thresholds are EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods, sales for consumption on the premises, and accommodation activities, and EUR 37,500 for services, with enhanced thresholds and annual legislative or indexation changes possible. A business exceeding the relevant thresholds must register and charge VAT from the legally prescribed date. For intra-EU B2C distance sales and certain electronically supplied services, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold may apply, with taxation in the customer Member State and possible use of the Union or non-Union One Stop Shop (OSS). Imports, intra-Community acquisitions, reverse-charge transactions, and certain cross-border supplies can create registration or reporting obligations independently of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved private platforms (Plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, or PDPs) and the public directory infrastructure. The reform is not a general real-time invoice-clearance system for all transactions: invoices are transmitted through the designated platform chain, while the DGFiP receives required invoice data and e-reporting data. Under the scheduled timetable, all French businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations apply to large and intermediate-sized businesses from 1 September 2026 and to small and medium-sized businesses, including most SAS entities, from 1 September 2027, subject to any statutory amendments or permitted extensions. Domestic B2B transactions within the French VAT scope are the principal target. B2C transactions and transactions with foreign businesses generally fall within e-reporting rather than domestic B2B e-invoicing where the statutory conditions are met. The system requires structured invoice data, mandated invoice fields, platform connectivity, and transmission of transaction and payment-status information where applicable. There is currently no universal French requirement for prior real-time fiscal clearance or a digital tax stamp on every invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU may be invoiced without French VAT under Article 262 I of the French Tax Code where the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by the seller or by an eligible customer or intermediary and the exporter retains legally sufficient evidence of exit from the EU customs territory. The supply must be correctly identified in the accounting records and export documentation. For a print-on-demand apparel business, the treatment depends on the actual supply chain: goods shipped from France directly to a non-EU destination may qualify; goods produced and shipped from another country may be outside the French VAT scope or subject to the rules of the production or dispatch country; and goods shipped to an EU customer are generally intra-Community supplies or domestic-distance-sale transactions rather than exports. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France may be outside the scope of French VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule, rather than technically zero-rated. B2C services and electronically supplied services require separate place-of-supply analysis. Refunds or deductions of input VAT require valid invoices, business-purpose evidence, and a direct link to taxable transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration submitted through the applicable French customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory, including the exit results or equivalent electronic exit evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, values, Incoterms where applicable, and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, airway bill, consignment note, or carrier delivery record
Proof linking the goods, export declaration, invoice, and transport movement, including order and fulfillment records for print-on-demand transactions
Customs EORI number and any applicable import, export, product, textile, or origin documentation
Proof of payment or other commercial evidence where needed to corroborate the transaction; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a French statutory condition for export VAT exemption
Accounting records and VAT return reconciliation supporting the zero-rated export amount
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days, and no general French foreign-exchange rule imposes a universal 180-day deadline for retaining export zero-rating. Export VAT exemption may be denied or retrospectively clawed back where the taxpayer cannot substantiate exit, misstates the customer or destination, uses inconsistent customs and accounting data, or applies export treatment to goods that did not leave the EU. The DGFiP may assess unpaid VAT, applicable late-payment interest, and penalties under the French Tax Code. Penalties may include a 40% increase for deliberate non-compliance and an 80% increase for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Additional penalties may apply for inaccurate VAT returns, failure to issue compliant invoices, customs violations, false declarations, or obstruction of an audit. Serious intentional VAT fraud can also create criminal exposure. The taxpayer should retain customs exit evidence, invoices, transport records, order and fulfillment data, customer evidence, payment records, and VAT reconciliations for the applicable French accounting and tax limitation periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank), together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) as the foreign exchange regulatory authority, and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the banking supervisory and licensing authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under the free movement of capital within the European Union and is an IMF Article VIII member; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no domestic exchange control licences or segregation requirements affecting profit remittances, loan repayments, or the repatriation of capital for a French SAS. Practical compliance hurdles include: (i) balance-of-payments reporting for every cross-border transaction above EUR 12,500, transmitted by the resident intermediary bank to the Banque de France; (ii) anti-money-laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) file requirements that may delay inbound/outbound remittances; (iii) the availability of distributable reserves in the statutory accounts before any profit repatriation; and (iv) French dividend withholding taxes or other final withholding charges unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. The treasury plan should therefore pre-clear non-resident shareholder remittance instruments with the French bank and ensure that all statutory tax and accounting requirements are met before cash is moved overseas.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any mandatory surrender, conversion, or minimum repatriation ratio on export receipts, including in respect of print-on-demand merchandise sales. Export proceeds may be held in non-euro currencies in ordinary foreign-currency accounts. The only regulatory requirement is declarative: exporters must ensure that the collection of export receivables, carried out via a licensed French credit institution or an authorized payment institution, is reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes when the transaction amount or the aggregate monthly cross-border receipts reaches or exceeds EUR 12,500. There is no specific conversion deadline, no obligation to sell foreign currency to the central bank, and no restriction on reinvesting overseas earnings; hedging is permitted to manage currency risk.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: CIC – Crédit Industriel et Commercial S.A.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, with material legal constraints. An EU/EEA licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) may provide account services, payment processing, cross-currency conversion and merchant acquiring in France under the single passport mechanism, following ACPR notification and registration. Such an EMI can support the treasury needs of a POD apparel SAS for low-value payouts, supplier transfers, and multi-currency balances. By contrast, an offshore digital EMI (e.g., domiciled in Singapore, the United Kingdom, or the United States without a French/EU licence) cannot accept deposits from French residents or issue French IBANs; it may only be used as a downstream payment/processing vehicle for non-French flows. The primary liquidity record and capital account must remain with a full French or EU-licensed credit institution to preserve access to SEPA, SWIFT, French tax authority portals, and to guarantee the availability of corporate banking services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute legal mandate exists that all directors and UBOs physically appear at a French branch for a low-risk, retail-stage SAS. French AML law permits remote onboarding through certified video-identification and electronic signature solutions. However, for an SAS controlled by non-resident UBOs or by a foreign parent, tier-1 banks generally require at least one physical appointment with a director or an authorised representative and, in practice, a face-to-face (or virtual) interview immediately after the preliminary KYC review. If the company operates without any French operational facility, the bank may require certified true copies of passports, proof of address, apostilled corporate documents and a French legal opinion. A physical interview at a main corporate banking centre is strongly advised because it reduces account-opening timelines, clarifies the POD business model, and enables direct dialogue on purpose codes and prohibited transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs or parent entities seated in jurisdictions included in the FATF grey list or with abnormal corporate complexity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Preparation of: (i) the French SAS's Kbis extract and RBE (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing; (ii) the UBO register with percentage of ownership and control; (iii) certified passport copies and residential proofs for every UBO; (iv) a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letter supported by tax returns, sale agreements, and notarial deeds; (v) reference letters from the UBO's current or previous banks; (vi) a signed group structure chart and (vii) an opinion letter from an admitted French / cross-border counsel explaining the economic rationale for the French SAS and the absence of high-risk indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Print-on-demand business model perceived as 'asset-light' with no physical warehouse, low capitalization, and a reliance on foreign subcontractors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Construct a comprehensive business file containing: (i) a granular business plan and financial model covering transaction volumes, average order values, and gross margins; (ii) signed service agreements with POD fulfillment partners (e.g., Printful, Printify, or a French/European atelier), detailing storage, printing, drop-shipping and returns handling; (iii) the full catalogue and e-commerce platform agreements (Shopify, Etsy, Amazon, Stripe, PayPal); (iv) due-diligence packs on major suppliers presenting their legal registration, trade references, and anti-trust/AML representation; (v) a cybersecurity/PCI-DSS compliance summary for the merchant processing environment; and (vi) a rationally prepared cash-flow forecast that validates the need for the requested facilities and volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volumes of small inbound cross-border payments from card / payment-aggregator networks in multiple currencies, potentially triggering frequency-scenario monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The corporate file should include: (i) a merchant-account statement history (3-6 months, if available) reconciled to the satisfaction of the onboarding bank; (ii) an explanation of chargeback/refund cycles and the process used to escalate suspected fraudulent transactions; (iii) operational procedures for AML and customer due-diligence on online buyers; (iv) evidence of adherence to the merchant aggregator's reserves and pay-out cycles; (v) a summary of the platform's anti-fraud controls, including CAPTCHA, 3-D Secure, and velocity checks; and (vi) formal declarations confirming that no proceeds are derived from prohibited goods/services under the bank's policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office located at a commercial domiciliation provider with no identifiable physical headquarters or staff on site.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) a legally binding domiciliation agreement with a licensed provider, issued under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code; (ii) a letter from the domiciliation provider certifying that it has received all correspondence and has the right to accept service on behalf of the company; (iii) evidence of the director's remote-work organisational structure, including accounting firm, lawyers and trade consultants; (iv) utility bills, lease or ownership evidence for any home office or actual operational address used by the management team; and (v) minutes confirming board approval of the registered office and delegation of mail-handling authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an SAS, cash contributions must be deposited, prior to registration, in a blocked account opened in the name of the company in formation or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC), unless the articles of incorporation provide for a contribution in kind. The inward wire should be transmitted through the international banking system using SWIFT MT103 (for non-SEPA) or SEPA Credit Transfer (for EU), utilising the recipient bank's IBAN/BIC and referencing: 'APPORT EN CAPITAL – [SAS legal name] – STATUTS [date]'. The sending bank must include the corporate KYC/reference file and, in the payment instructions, the purpose code for direct investment / capital subscription under Banque de France's balance-of-payments classification. The receiving French bank will release the funds after verifying the company's registry excerpt and the constitution signatures against the attestation du dépositaire des fonds. All transfers from non-EU sources must be subjected to sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening before the funds are made available. For non-EU injection via an agency arrangement, a specific order should be filed using the 'capitaux / apport' reporting code and the underlying transaction documents (constitutive deed, statutory auditor's or notary's statement) retained in the bank's DDA file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for a POD custom apparel enterprise should be structured as follows: (i) for EU/EEA suppliers and logistics settlements, use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with ISO 20022 pain.001 payment initiation, through the French corporate banking portal, including the invoice number, RCS/SIRET identifiers, and a clear description of goods; (ii) for non-EU suppliers in GBP, CHF, USD, CNY, or other convertible currencies, use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer with the BIC/IBAN or bank free-format code and the payment reference = commercial invoice + PO; (iii) for high-value or strategic procurements where open-account risk is unacceptable, a Commercial Letter of Credit may be issued in accordance with UCP 600 and the ISBP 745, with a confirmed/advised beneficiary; (iv) the French forwarder/broker may process import/export clearing through the national VAT portal, and the bank will report cross-border outbound payments above the EUR 12,500 threshold. No exchange-control authorisation is required for any outbound trade payment, but complete invoice documentation and the underlying trade contract must remain in the corporate treasury file and be produced within the statutory AML retention period.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR vs major trade currencies: USD, GBP, CNY, CHF, JPY) with a licensed counterparty under an ISDA Agreement or a French counterparty standard annex

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with implied settlement restrictions or limited offshore deliverability, including CNH/INR/BRL equivalents, locked under ACPR-regulated credit institutions
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) combining principal and interest exchanges for any material cross-border financing or large supplier arrangement
FX Options and collars (costless zero-premium structures) in the institutional market, subject to bank credit approval and EMIR clearing/obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' decision approving the annual financial statements and discharging the president (written consultation or minutes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS corporate records — maintained at the registered office / corporate agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of each fiscal year; extendable only by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold or record the approval can expose the president to injunctive relief by the commercial court and prevents the lawful filing of the annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (comptes annuels) together with the management report and shareholders' approval minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce via the INPI national formalities window (Guichet des formalités des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholders' approval; approval is due within six months of the fiscal year-end, so a 31 December year-end must be filed by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit may lead to court-ordered astreinte (up to EUR 1,500 per day of delay), monetary penalties, and after repeated non-compliance, administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax package (liasse fiscale) and annual tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, file on the second business day after 1 May under the official DGFiP calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a late-filing surcharge, monthly late-payment interest and, in the case of intentional omission, penalties of up to 40% of the outstanding corporate income tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) accuracy refresh / modification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / RCS through the INPI formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership; no separate annual filing if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or inaccurate declaration is a criminal offence sanctionable by fines and, for legal representatives, potential imprisonment; repeat breaches can be recorded against the entity in the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit for an SAS is required when, on the balance-sheet date, at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: total balance-sheet assets > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average permanent headcount > 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (ANC regulation 2016-07) for SAS statutory annual accounts; IFRS as adopted in the EU is permitted for consolidated or voluntary reporting, not for the standard individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require an annual stand-alone UBO return. The registered beneficial-owner declaration must be updated with the RCS within 30 days of any share transfer or change of control; as part of the annual record-keeping calendar, the SAS should obtain written confirmation from each registered UBO so the statutory register mirrors the filed declaration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,200 per year for commercial domiciliation services; USD 600 - 2,000 per year for a full corporate agent/registered-office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 8,000 per year for a small SAS with simple accounts, increasing if a formal statutory audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for SMEs meeting turnover and ownership conditions; Research Tax Credit (CIR) 30% on eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) 20% on eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000; territoriality principle for foreign PE income; family-owned group taxation option.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa n° 2065-SD (income tax return) and annexes 2031-A, 2033-A, 2059-A, 2069-SD; filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel / EFI télédéclaration).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year aligned to accounting period)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December: file by the second working day after 3 May of the following year. For non-calendar fiscal years: file within three months of the closing date of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after accounting result adjustments (reintégrations, déductions, déficits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only French-source taxable profit attributable to the French permanent establishment or directly derived from French activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carried forward from prior years available to offset current taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only the deductible carryforward computed under Article 209 CGI; attach reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits such as CIR, CII, apprenticeship tax credit, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only credits attributable to French-source income or French permanent establishment; attach supporting computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 3.3% social contribution on the amount of corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess only if the French tax base of the PE exceeds the threshold; treaty credit does not eliminate the surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of fixed asset depreciation for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Depreciate only assets held by the French permanent establishment and used for French-source business; transfer pricing consistency required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic increase of the assessed taxes if filed within 30 days of a formal demand; 40% increase for bad faith; 80% increase for a deliberate fraudulent manoeuvre; late-payment interest accrues at 0.2% per month. A flat penalty of EUR 150 applies for each omitted or inaccurate annex. Directors may be jointly liable for repeated non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic rate: 30% for non-resident individuals (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies); 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders. Treaty rates may reduce to 0%, 5% or 15% depending on shareholding and residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before dividend payment, the beneficial owner must submit to the French paying agent a completed Cerfa n° 5057 form (for reduced withholding at source) together with the foreign tax residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) and statement of beneficial ownership. If treaty relief is not granted at source, apply for a refund to the French tax authority (DRFIP) before 31 December of the second year following the distribution year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax 33.33% on gross payments for use of patents, trademarks, know-how and copyrights; income tax treaties generally reduce to 0%–10% depending on the nature of the IP and beneficial ownership. Interest: no general domestic withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents, except for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or profit-sharing bonds; treaties usually provide 0%–10% rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are required when a French entity or its global group has consolidated turnover or total assets equal to or exceeding EUR 400 million (Article L.13 AA and L.13 AB CGI). All other taxpayers must retain contemporaneous TP documentation sufficient to justify intra-group prices in an audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but applies substance-oriented doctrines: tax residence requires actual management in France; Article L.64 CGI (abus de droit) permits recharacterising arrangements lacking genuine economic substance; treaty benefits require beneficial ownership and an active business purpose. A SAS must show real staff, decisions and expenditure—a shell or pass-through holding cannot claim treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of taxable profits, falsifying books, booking fictitious POD production costs, or under-reporting digital commerce sales on Stripe/PayPal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 (or 50% of the evaded sum) and imprisonment up to 5 years; administrative penalty of 80% on understated tax plus late-payment interest; loss of tax credits and forfeiture of seized assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who materially participates in fraudulent filing can be criminally convicted and held civilly liable for the evaded tax and penalties; in aggravated cases the court may impose a travel ban, professional prohibition, and freezing of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit Cerfa n° 2065-SD and annexes by the statutory deadline without valid justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% automatic tax increase if filed after a formal notice; 40% increase for bad faith; 80% increase for fraudulent behaviour; late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; flat EUR 150 penalty per missing annex.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Persistent non-filing allows the administration to sue directors personally for collection of penalties if the company is insolvent and non-filing constitutes gross management misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of law / artificial shell structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SAS or interposed foreign entity lacking employees, premises, real decision-making or business purpose, used exclusively to shift profits through inflated inter-company payments or artificial licensing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 80% or 100% of the recharacterised tax advantage (Article L.64 CGI), plus interest; the structure is disregarded and the true taxpayer is reassessed; third-party fines up to EUR 10,000 may apply to colluding advisors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly set up and operate an artificial structure are personally exposed to reinstatement (remise en cause), joint liability for sanctions, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud; travel bans can be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-corporate personal Stripe or PayPal accounts to collect corporate POd sales, commingling funds, or failing to identify beneficial owners, leading to illegal concealment of revenue or money-laundering vulnerability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties under the French Monetary and Financial Code up to EUR 375,000 for individuals and EUR 750,000 for legal entities; business ban for payment-service providers; criminal money-laundering conviction up to 5 years’ imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed to personal fines, restitution orders, freezing orders, and travel restrictions; under AML provisions a managing director can be prohibited from exercising managerial functions for up to 10 years.
